title: Regular-functorial normalized resolution rules
statement: Use the rational quasi-excellent resolution inputs of [def-per-qe-ordinary-resolution-rule]: an input is a reduced Noetherian scheme $X$ over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth], such that every affine coordinate ring is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. A morphism is regular in the sense of [def-per-qe-ordinary-resolution-rule]: it is flat and its fibres stay regular after every finite extension of the residue fields, that is, it has geometrically regular fibres. A normalized resolution over $X$ is a finite normalized blowup tower [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization], with an initial isomorphism to $X$, nonempty nowhere dense center zero schemes, and regular last scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Its centers are the actual coherent ideal sheaves. A regular pullback is a tower of the same length with regular level maps, all extended center ideals, commuting arrows and cartesian squares over level zero [def-per-normalized-tower-descent-data]. A regular resolution comparison identifies the source resolution with the contraction of this pullback over the specified base morphism. Contraction is the existing ordered contraction: it deletes exactly unit-center isomorphism stages, retaining a nontrivial normalization. A regular-functorial normalized resolution rule assigns a resolution to every input and such a comparison to every regular morphism over $\mathbf Q$. Comparisons satisfy identity and composition equations on both indices and actual level maps. All inputs are included, in particular finite disjoint unions and the empty scheme.
